feedback: Pre-race review. Nothing has raced for this candidate, so this states no outcome for it. The candidate is valid: five sensors match five weights, all x-positions are within ±0.08 m, y = 0.03 m is in range, and every controller field is inside its limit. It changes one group from the best raced design (iteration 5, score 41.1832): the outer sensors move from ±0.06 to ±0.07 m, with weights unchanged (outer ±1.5, inner ±0.75, centre 0). base_speed is 1.4, kp 2.5, ki 0.5, kd 0.2 and line_loss last_direction, all matching iteration 5. The evidence behind the geometry change: iteration 1 (±0.04 m) and iteration 2 (±0.06 m) show that the wider span removed line loss (1 loss per run to 0), but max_error stayed pinned at about 0.061 in every iteration, and iterations 3 to 6 moved kp, ki, kd and base_speed with little effect. Every run has ended off_track, with max_error sitting just above the fixed 0.06 m limit. Because max(0.06, tape_half_width + body_width/4) equals 0.06 for any body_width up to 0.18 m, body geometry cannot widen the tolerance, so the lever is sensing and steering. The pinned error with no line loss points to the robot leaving the line steadily rather than losing sight of it, so ±0.07 is a mild test with limited upside. Its main risk is that the outer sensor reacts later on tight bends, which could lower progress. Approve because it is a clean single-group test of the best design, it costs one race run, and the telemetry will be more useful than another round of reading numbers. After the race, use the telemetry as follows. (a) If line_loss_events stays 0, max_error stays at or above 0.06 and progress is flat (s-bend near 0.041, slalom near 0.035), the sensor span is not the limit; stop widening and test controller.ki or kp in a single step, since neither moved max_error before. (b) If progress falls below 0.041 on the s-bend or below 0.035 on the slalom, return the outer sensors to ±0.06 (iteration 5). (c) If max_error falls below 0.06 with progress rising, keep ±0.07 and test base_speed 1.3 next to recover completion time.
requested_changes: After the race, if progress falls below iteration 5's 0.0409 (s-bend) or 0.035 (slalom), set geometry.sensor_positions outer x back to ±0.06 and keep the other fields, since iteration 5 is the best raced design at 41.1832.

If line_loss_events is 0 and max_error stays at or above 0.06 with flat progress, change one controller field only (for example ki from 0.5 to 2.0 cap test, or kp from 2.5 to 2.0) and keep the ±0.07 span, citing iterations 3 to 6 where kp, ki and kd each moved the score by under 0.5.

If max_error falls below 0.06 with progress rising, keep the ±0.07 span and set controller.base_speed to 1.3 with other fields unchanged, to recover completion time without the 1.2 slip seen in iteration 6.
